checks.approve-branch: node --test --test-name-pattern="approve on a job's branch" test/approve-anywhere.test.mjs
checks.adr-branch: node --test --test-name-pattern="adr accept on a job's branch" test/approve-anywhere.test.mjs

jobs.goal: setup honours --runs-on on GitHub too
jobs.brief: setup.mjs only passes runsOn to the workflow for Gitea; on GitHub the workflow always says ubuntu-latest. Pass it for GitHub, and make doctor flag a workflow whose runs-on differs from the runner the person chose (or a self-hosted label with no runner).

done_when.text: setup --runs-on <label> on a GitHub repo writes runs-on: <label>
doctor reports a self-hosted label that no runner carries

jobs.goal: gmod commit stages only the job's own files
jobs.brief: commitJob runs git add -A, so nested repositories (e.g. agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees) and stray files end up committed as gitlinks. Stage exactly the files the last green check ran on, within the job's files and tests, plus its journal; never gitlinks.

done_when.text: a nested git repository in the worktree is not committed
an untracked file outside the job is not committed
a file deleted or renamed inside the job is still committed

jobs.goal: A CI change can be made as a planned job
jobs.brief: The gate passes a CI change only when it carries CI files alone, but a job always adds its journal and a test, so no job can change CI. Let a job whose files are all CI/governance files land as a governance change: its journal is allowed, and its check may be a governance check under .gmod/ rather than a test file. Keep: CI changes never mixed with code.

done_when.text: a job changing only the workflow passes the gate as a governance change
a job mixing workflow and code is still refused

jobs.goal: pr --status works on GitHub
jobs.brief: prStatus throws on anything but Gitea. Read the PR's checks and the gate's and review's reports through gh on GitHub (and glab on GitLab if cheap), so agents can follow their pull requests with mcp__gmod__pr_status.

done_when.text: pr --status on a GitHub repo reports the checks and both reports from recorded gh output

jobs.goal: Branches gmod catches up get checked without a person
jobs.brief: After a landing, CI merges main into open job branches as github-actions[bot]; GitHub then holds those pull_request runs as action_required, so they wait for a person. After a catch-up, start the gate through repository_dispatch (already in the workflow) for that branch, or push as the GitHub App when one is set, so no run needs approval. (doctor-catch-up-path reports which path is in use.)

done_when.text: a catch-up dispatches a gate run for the branch instead of relying on the bot push
a branch is not checked twice for the same commit

jobs.goal: gmod state --json prints the plan and its progress
jobs.brief: DESIGN E1 (in ~/skiff/DESIGN.md 6.3, 6.4): a state record {v:1, project, plan (phases, backlog, voyages when present), jobs with state, modality if declared, ruleset if any, activity} built from plan.json, claims, main's history and the journal. Skiff already reads this shape from recordings: match ~/skiff/crates/skiff-host/tests/fixtures/gmod/v1/state/*.json, which define the contract.

done_when.text: state --json on a test repo lists phases, jobs and their states
a job with a landed <job>: commit shows as proven

jobs.goal: gmod signals --json lists what needs a person
jobs.brief: DESIGN E1 and D9/D10: move the pane's Needs-you logic (hooks/register.tsx) into lib/signals.mjs, computed from state, never stored; each signal has a stable id (hash of its cause), kind decide|unstick|know, a plain question, evidence and actions. The pane then calls the same function. Match the shape in ~/skiff/crates/skiff-host/tests/fixtures/gmod/v1/signals/*.json.

done_when.text: a pending proposal and a stuck job each give a signal with a stable id
a resolved cause no longer gives its signal
the pane shows the same Needs-you items as before on recorded cases

jobs.goal: gmod capabilities --json says what this gmod speaks
jobs.brief: DESIGN E2 and 6.5: {v:1, engine:"gmod", version, protocol:"1.0", enforcers:[...], managed: true|false (this gmod supports managed mode), presets?, inventory?}. A face uses it to know which managed features exist before offering them. Match ~/skiff/crates/skiff-host/tests/fixtures/gmod/v1/gmod.

done_when.text: capabilities --json prints the version, protocol 1.x and the enforcers

jobs.goal: A per-repo switch for managed features, off by default
jobs.brief: Managed mode is where face-driven features (voyages, requests, decide, packs) will live; this job adds only the switch. .gmod/managed.json {v:1, managed:true} written as a governance decision by `gmod manage on|off` (a person, never an agent; refused from an agent identity), read by `gmod manage status`. state --json reports managed:true|false. When off (the default, and when the file is absent) nothing in the plan format, pane, gate or commands changes: prove it by running the existing suite against a repo with the switch off. See the ADR on managed features.

done_when.text: gmod manage on writes .gmod/managed.json as a decision and state --json says managed: true
an agent identity is refused
with the switch off, the existing test suite passes unchanged

jobs.goal: The gate runs once per pull request commit
jobs.brief: When a held github-actions[bot] pull_request run (action_required) is approved after gmod already dispatched a gate run for the same head, the gate and review run twice. In ci/action.mjs, before gating a pull request, look up the head commit's statuses; if gmod/gate (the gate's context) already reported for that sha, skip gate, review and land for this run and say so in the summary. A new head commit is gated as usual.

done_when.text: a head whose gmod/gate status already exists is not gated again
a head with no gate status is gated as before

jobs.goal: doctor says how caught-up branches get checked
jobs.brief: In lib/setup.mjs doctor (GitHub): report which catch-up path is in use — the GitHub App (app-id/app-key in the workflow, so its pushes start runs) or repository_dispatch (the workflow takes gmod events) — and flag neither as ✗ with its fix (gmod setup). Gitea and GitLab are unchanged.

done_when.text: doctor names the GitHub App path when the workflow has app keys
doctor names repository_dispatch otherwise, and flags a workflow with neither

jobs.goal: npm test runs every test file
jobs.brief: package.json's test script lists files by hand, so setup-runs-on, commit-files, pr-status, catch-up, ci-change-job (and future) tests never run in CI. Run every test/*.test.mjs (review-live skips itself without a key). Add test/suite.test.mjs asserting the script covers every test/*.test.mjs on disk. test/cli.test.mjs: 'a plan can start from nothing' sets user.email but no user.name, so it fails on a runner with no global git identity (the gate's); give it a name.

done_when.text: npm test's script covers every test/*.test.mjs
the whole suite passes

jobs.goal: Release gmod 1.5.0 so repos can upgrade
jobs.brief: Bump package.json, package-lock.json and .claude-plugin/plugin.json to 1.5.0 and start CHANGELOG.md with a 1.5.0 entry listing the Fixes phase. Once it lands, the v1.5.0 tag is pushed on that commit (image.yml checks it matches package.json), which is what gmod ci upgrade looks for.

done_when.text: package.json, package-lock.json and plugin.json all say 1.5.0, and CHANGELOG.md has a 1.5.0 entry

jobs.goal: The Bash hook gates commits without rewriting commands
jobs.brief: hooks/register.tsx:328 puts a git() shell function in front of every Bash command whose text contains the word "commit" (gated(), line 107). Auto mode reviewed the original command, sees a different one, and gives no verdict, so calls have to be sent again; harmless commands like `grep commit` are rewritten too. Instead: a parser in hooks/shell.ts (beside movesClaims etc.) finds whether the command runs `git commit` and in which directory (`git -C dir commit`, `cd dir && git commit`, global options skipped as gated() does today). If it does, the hook runs `gmod gate-commit --dir <dir>` itself before next(): a refusal becomes deny with the gate's text, a pass runs the command exactly as written. Every other command runs unchanged. Remove gated(). Not in scope: commits hidden inside scripts or make targets (the shell function caught those; a git pre-commit hook could later), and the Edit/Write guards, which never rewrite.

done_when.text: a command that only mentions commit, or runs no git commit, reaches the shell exactly as written
git commit and git -C <dir> commit run the commit gate in the hook for that dir: a refusal denies the call, a pass runs the command unchanged
a command that runs git commit and also anything but cd and git (an edit, eval, a function) is refused, so what is committed is what the gate saw

jobs.goal: Approving works from any branch, even a job's
jobs.brief: approve (lib/core.mjs:1186) writes .gmod/plan.json and commits it on the checked-out branch, so it refuses a gmod/ job branch (line 1191); adr accept does the same (lib/adr.mjs:145). A person approving from a session that is working a job (its folder on gmod/<job>, or a job worktree) is refused every time. Instead, build the decision commit off the checkout: on main's tip (local main, or origin/main when that is ahead), with a temporary index (read-tree, hash-object, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree), and hand that commit to publishDecision (lib/ci.mjs:591), which today pushes HEAD, so it pushes the given commit as gmod/plan-<sha> / the decision branch. The proposal's base is checked against the plan in that main commit, not the job branch's copy. The checkout, its index and its branch are never touched; when the checkout is on main itself, it still moves to the new commit as today. test/cli.test.mjs ('the agent drafts the plan, a person approves it, and it lands alone', line ~429) asserts that approve on a job's branch is refused; rewrite that part so approve on a job's branch succeeds and leaves the checkout alone, keeping its approve-from-main path. Not in scope: the pane's wording, and plan branches other than main.

done_when.text: approve on a job's branch commits the plan on main's tip, publishes it, and leaves the checkout, index and branch as they were
approve on main behaves as before
adr accept on a job's branch works the same way

jobs.goal: Subagent prompts are never changed by gmod's hook
jobs.brief: hooks/register.tsx ~line 336: in a governed repository, an Agent call whose prompt lacks FOR_SUBAGENTS gets it appended (next({ ...e, prompt: e.prompt + FOR_SUBAGENTS })). Auto mode reviewed the original prompt, sees a changed one and gives no verdict, so the call has to be sent again. Instead, deny such a call with a message that says the subagent needs gmod's routine and quotes FOR_SUBAGENTS to add to the prompt verbatim; a prompt that already carries it passes unchanged, as today. Ungoverned repositories: unchanged. With this and bash-hook-no-rewrite, no gmod hook changes a tool call's input. Not in scope: the routine's wording.

done_when.text: in a governed repository, an Agent prompt without the routine is refused with the routine to add, and nothing runs
a prompt that carries the routine, or any Agent call in an ungoverned repository, runs exactly as written

jobs.goal: A commit bundled with file changes is refused
jobs.brief: bash-hook-no-rewrite landed (PR #17) before its third criterion's code, when the npx check let its gate pass: the commit gate now runs in the hook before the command, so `echo x >> f && git commit -am x` commits what the gate never saw. Add commitsAlone(cmd) to hooks/shell.ts: a command that runs git commit may beside it only cd/pushd/popd and git add/commit/status/diff/log/show/rev-parse, with no redirection into a file and no $(…) beyond cat/printf (heredoc messages); a commit inside eval, sh/bash -c, xargs, source or a shell function is refused. The hook denies such a command with 'a commit runs on its own' before gating. The reader keeps heredoc bodies as one word and reads 2>&1 / &> as redirections. The code is written on gmod/bash-hook-no-rewrite (PR #23, refused because that job is done); carry it over.

done_when.text: a command that runs git commit and also anything but cd and quiet git (an edit, eval, sh -c, a function) is refused before it runs
a commit with git add, cd, a heredoc message or 2>&1 still runs exactly as written

jobs.goal: The gate lands a managed switch like a plan change
jobs.brief: gmod manage on|off commits .gmod/managed.json alone on a gmod/managed-<on|off>-<sha> branch (lib/managed.mjs, PR #32), but core.verify has no case for it: it reads the branch as a job named managed-on-<sha> and refuses it. Teach verify to judge a pull request that changes only .gmod/managed.json as a person's decision, the way it judges a plan or ADR change: it travels alone (mixed with any other file it is refused), and it gets the governance review. Don't change how plan, ADR, CI or job pull requests are judged.

done_when.text: a pull request changing only .gmod/managed.json passes the gate as a decision
a pull request mixing .gmod/managed.json with any other file is refused
the whole suite passes

jobs.goal: An agent's shell cannot run gmod manage on or off
jobs.brief: decidesPlan in hooks/shell.ts refuses an agent running gmod approve/reject/adr accept from its shell, but not gmod manage on|off, and an agent at the keyboard commits as the person, so lib/managed.mjs's identity check can't catch it. Extend decidesPlan to match gmod manage on and gmod manage off; plain gmod manage and gmod manage status (read-only) must still run.

done_when.text: gmod manage on and gmod manage off from an agent's shell are refused
gmod manage and gmod manage status still run

jobs.goal: The reviewer reviews managed switches; the refusal names them
jobs.brief: Two loose ends from managed-gate and managed-hook. (1) ci/review.mjs (~line 133) decides governance with f === core.PLAN || adr prefix || core.isCiFile(f), so a pull request changing only .gmod/managed.json gets 'skipped (no job named)': the gate passes it and nothing reviews it. Count core.MANAGED_SWITCH as governance too. (2) hooks/register.tsx (~line 339): when decidesPlan refuses gmod manage on|off, the agent is told 'approving or rejecting the plan is the person's decision'; name managed mode for those commands (shell.ts exports switchesManaged). Approve/reject wording stays as is.

done_when.text: a pull request changing only .gmod/managed.json gets the governance review
an agent refused gmod manage on|off is told it is the person's managed-mode decision
the whole suite passes

jobs.goal: Release gmod 1.6.0 so Skiff can use the new commands
jobs.brief: Bump to 1.6.0 as release-1-5-0 did: `npm version 1.6.0 --no-git-tag-version` (package.json, package-lock.json root and packages[""]), plugin.json by hand, and point test/release.test.mjs at 1.6.0. Add a CHANGELOG.md 1.6.0 entry above 1.5.0, plain-English impact first with a few tech details (commands, files, PR numbers): gmod state/signals/capabilities --json for faces like Skiff (#29, #30, #31); the managed-mode switch, person-only, gated and reviewed (#32, #34, #35, #37); the pane's Needs-you now comes from lib/signals.mjs. After landing, the person tags v1.6.0 on the landed commit and publishes the release.

done_when.text: package.json, package-lock.json and plugin.json all say 1.6.0, and CHANGELOG.md has a 1.6.0 entry

jobs.goal: CI runs gmod 1.6.0 instead of 1.4.7
jobs.brief: Change `uses: soundheart-studios/gmod@v1.4.7` to `@v1.6.0` in .github/workflows/gmod.yml (line 16), nothing else. This brings 1.5.0's CI fixes (catch-up dispatch once per commit, no double gate) and 1.6.0's managed-switch gate and review into CI. It lands as a CI change made by a job (CI files only).

done_when.text: the gmod workflow uses soundheart-studios/gmod@v1.6.0

jobs.goal: The hook refuses decisions, not commands that mention them
jobs.brief: decidesPlan in hooks/shell.ts still matches approve/reject/accept with a regex anywhere in the command, so a read-only `grep 'gmod approve' test/mod.test.tsx` was refused (seen in managed-review). Read approve/reject/adr accept word by word with the same quote-aware reader switchesManaged already uses, so only a real gmod approve/reject/adr accept command is refused. Export switchesManaged (or a decision-kind helper) and use it in hooks/register.tsx instead of the APPROVES regex copied there in managed-review. Refusal wording stays as is.

done_when.text: a command that only mentions gmod approve, reject or adr accept (grep, echo, a commit message) runs
gmod approve, gmod reject and gmod adr accept run from an agent's shell are still refused, with the same words

phases.title: Fixes
phases.outcome: Setting up and running gmod on GitHub works without hand edits or a person approving each run.

phases.title: Contract for faces
phases.outcome: A face like Skiff can read gmod's version, state and signals as JSON, without the pane.

phases.title: Managed mode
phases.outcome: A repository can opt into managed features (for faces like Skiff) with one switch; without it, gmod behaves exactly as before.

phases.title: Managed guard
phases.outcome: Only a person can switch managed mode, and the switch's own pull request lands through the gate.

phases.title: Upkeep
phases.outcome: CI runs gmod 1.6.0, and gmod's hook refuses only real decisions, not commands that mention them.
